plan.title: docs+ingest: document sliced leans and the deft-slice child-issue route; name it in the refusal

narratives.Description: docs+ingest: document sliced leans and the deft-slice child-issue route; name it in the refusal
narratives.Overview:
## Problem

When an accepted arc lean has a `## Slices` section, `issue:ingest` / `triage:accept` refuses the parent issue ("every harvested item of the cited lean belongs to a slice label -- nothing written"). The only route the code allows (#6333 item 6, `resolveSliceIngest` in `packages/core/src/intake/issue-ingest.ts`) is one child issue per slice whose body carries `deft-slice: #<parent> <label>`; each child ingests its slice from the parent's accepted lean and checks the Target-digest against the unedited parent body. None of this is described in `content/` or `docs/`, no verb creates slice issues, and the refusal does not name the remedy. A worker had to find it by reading the code (#7062, 2026-11-22).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The arc/ingest docs (design-critique contract or skill, and `content/commands.md` for `issue:ingest`) describe slices: when a lean should declare them, the `deft-slice: #<parent> <label>` child-issue line, that the parent body must stay unedited, and how briefs and PRs map to slices.
- [ ] The ingest refusal for a fully sliced lean names the remedy: file one child issue per slice label with the exact `deft-slice:` line, and lists the slice labels found.
- [ ] A verb (for example `deft issue:slice -- --parent <N> --label <label>`) or documented `gh issue create` recipe creates a correct child issue body from the lean's slice.
- [ ] The swarm and build skills mention slices where they describe ingest.

Refs #7062, #6333.

issueCommentThread.body: arc: not warranted, because the work documents an existing mechanism (#6333 item 6, `resolveSliceIngest`), adds the remedy to one refusal message, and documents a `gh issue create` recipe for child issues. No new verb, gate or data shape, so there is no design fork to critique. Acceptance comes from the issue body's Acceptance Criteria list.
